items.headline: ISRO begins 2024 with XPoSat launch
items.detail: ISRO launched XPoSat, the X-ray Polarimeter Satellite, on PSLV-C58 on January 1, 2024 - only the world's second X-ray polarimetry observatory after NASA's IXPE - to study polarisation of cosmic X-rays from black holes and neutron stars.

items.headline: Twin bombings kill scores in Kerman, Iran
items.detail: Two suicide bombings near Qasem Soleimani's grave in Kerman, Iran, on January 3, 2024 - the fourth anniversary of his death - killed dozens and wounded nearly 300. The Islamic State claimed responsibility in the deadliest attack in Iran since 1978.

items.headline: India win shortest-ever Test at Cape Town
items.detail: India beat South Africa by 7 wickets in the second Test at Newlands, Cape Town, finished inside two days in just 642 balls - the shortest completed Test in history. Mohammed Siraj took 6/15 as South Africa fell for 55; the series ended 1-1.

items.headline: Aditya-L1 reaches halo orbit around L1
items.detail: ISRO's Aditya-L1, India's first dedicated solar mission, was inserted into a halo orbit around Lagrange point 1 on January 6, 2024, about 1.5 million km from Earth - a gravitationally stable spot giving a continuous view of the Sun.

items.headline: Sheikh Hasina wins fourth straight term in Bangladesh
items.detail: The Awami League won 224 of 300 seats in Bangladesh's January 7, 2024 election, giving Sheikh Hasina a fourth consecutive term and fifth premiership overall. The BNP boycotted the poll and turnout fell to about 42%.

items.headline: 'Oppenheimer' leads Golden Globes
items.detail: 'Oppenheimer' won five awards including Best Motion Picture - Drama at the 81st Golden Globes on January 7, 2024, with Cillian Murphy winning Best Actor. Lily Gladstone became the first Indigenous acting winner at the Globes.

items.headline: PM inaugurates Atal Setu, India's longest sea bridge
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri-Nhava Sheva Atal Setu (Mumbai Trans Harbour Link) on January 12, 2024. The 21.8 km link - India's longest sea bridge - connects Sewri in Mumbai with Nhava Sheva, costing Rs 17,843 crore.

items.headline: Lai Ching-te wins Taiwan presidential election
items.detail: Lai Ching-te of the ruling DPP won Taiwan's presidential election on January 13, 2024 with about 40% of the vote, making the DPP the first party to win three consecutive presidencies since direct elections began in 1996. Hsiao Bi-khim is his vice president.

items.headline: Denmark's Queen Margrethe II abdicates
items.detail: Queen Margrethe II abdicated on January 14, 2024 after 52 years - Denmark's first voluntary abdication since 1146 - and her son became King Frederik X. Queen Mary is the first Australian-born queen consort of a European country.

items.headline: Sinner wins first Grand Slam at Australian Open
items.detail: Jannik Sinner won his first Grand Slam at the Australian Open (January 14-28, 2024), coming back from two sets down to beat Daniil Medvedev after ending Djokovic's streak in the semifinals. Aryna Sabalenka defended her women's title, beating Zheng Qinwen.

items.headline: Davos summit held on 'Rebuilding Trust' theme
items.detail: The World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting was held at Davos, Switzerland from January 15-19, 2024, under the theme 'Rebuilding Trust'.

items.headline: 'The Bear' and 'Succession' top delayed Emmys
items.detail: The 75th Primetime Emmy Awards, pushed to January 15, 2024 due to the Hollywood strikes, saw 'The Bear' and 'Succession' win six major awards each; Elton John became the 19th EGOT recipient.

items.headline: Japan's 'Moon Sniper' lands on the Moon
items.detail: JAXA's SLIM lander touched down near the Shioli crater on January 20, 2024 (JST), making Japan the fifth country to soft-land on the Moon after the USSR, USA, China and India. The precision 'Moon Sniper' landed nose-down and ran on limited battery before reviving later.
examFacts: Japan: 5th country to soft-land on Moon

items.headline: Ram Mandir consecration at Ayodhya
items.detail: The Pran Pratishtha of the Ram Lalla idol was performed at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya on January 22, 2024, with PM Narendra Modi officiating the consecration in the sanctum sanctorum. Only the temple's ground floor was opened; over half a million visitors came on the first day.

items.headline: India celebrates 75th Republic Day
items.detail: India celebrated its 75th Republic Day on January 26, 2024, with French President Emmanuel Macron as chief guest - the sixth French leader to get the honour - after a state visit.

items.headline: RBI bars Paytm Payments Bank from new deposits
items.detail: The RBI ordered Paytm Payments Bank to stop accepting fresh deposits, credit transactions and top-ups after February 29, 2024 - later extended to March 15 - citing persistent non-compliance under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act.

quiz.q: XPoSat, launched on January 1, 2024, is the world's ___ X-ray polarimetry observatory.
quiz.solution: Only NASA's IXPE (2021) preceded it; XPoSat launched on PSLV-C58.

quiz.q: On January 6, 2024, Aditya-L1 was placed in a halo orbit around:
quiz.solution: India's first solar mission settled at Lagrange point 1, about 1.5 million km from Earth.

quiz.q: Sheikh Hasina's January 2024 election win in Bangladesh was her ___ consecutive term.
quiz.solution: The Awami League won 224 of 300 seats for her fourth straight term (fifth overall).

quiz.q: Atal Setu, inaugurated in January 2024, is India's longest:
quiz.solution: The 21.8 km Mumbai Trans Harbour Link is India's longest sea bridge.

quiz.q: Who was the chief guest at India's 75th Republic Day parade on January 26, 2024?
quiz.solution: French President Emmanuel Macron attended after a state visit - the sixth French chief guest.

quiz.q: Japan became the ___ country to soft-land on the Moon when SLIM touched down in January 2024.
quiz.solution: SLIM landed after the USSR, USA, China and India; it is nicknamed 'Moon Sniper'.

quiz.q: The Ram Mandir's Pran Pratishtha at Ayodhya was performed on:
quiz.solution: PM Modi led the consecration of the Ram Lalla idol on January 22, 2024.

quiz.q: Who won their first Grand Slam title at the 2024 Australian Open men's singles?
quiz.solution: Sinner came back from two sets down against Medvedev for his first major.

quiz.q: The RBI's January 31, 2024 order barred which payments bank from accepting fresh deposits?
quiz.solution: Paytm Payments Bank faced the curbs under Section 35A for persistent non-compliance.

quiz.q: Denmark's Margrethe II abdicated in January 2024 after 52 years - the first voluntary abdication there since:
quiz.solution: King Frederik X succeeded her; the last voluntary Danish abdication was in 1146.

items.headline: Five Bharat Ratnas announced in 2024
items.detail: Five Bharat Ratnas were announced in February 2024 - Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, P.V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh and M.S. Swaminathan - four of them posthumous, taking the total recipients to 53.
examFacts: Only L.K. Advani among them is living

items.headline: Interim Budget 2024-25 presented
items.detail: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the interim Budget for 2024-25 on February 1, 2024 in the 17th Lok Sabha, ahead of the general election. Announcements included rooftop solar targeting 300 units of free electricity a month, three major railway corridors, and support for coal gasification and the EV ecosystem.

items.headline: Yashasvi Jaiswal scores first Test double century
items.detail: Twenty-two-year-old Yashasvi Jaiswal hit 209 - his first Test double century - in the second Test against England at Visakhapatnam, helping India win by 106 runs. Jasprit Bumrah reached 150 Test wickets in the same match.

items.headline: Grammys 2024: Taylor Swift sets Album of the Year record
items.detail: At the 66th Grammy Awards on February 4, 2024, Taylor Swift's 'Midnights' won Album of the Year, making her the first artist to win the category four times. Miley Cyrus' 'Flowers' took Record of the Year and Billie Eilish's 'What Was I Made For?' Song of the Year.

items.headline: Australia win Under-19 Cricket World Cup
items.detail: Australia beat defending champions India by 79 runs in the final in South Africa on February 11, 2024 to win their fourth ICC U-19 World Cup. South Africa's Kwena Maphaka was Player of the Tournament with 21 wickets.
examFacts: Final: Australia beat India by 79 runs
Player of the Tournament: Kwena Maphaka

items.headline: Alexander Stubb wins Finnish presidency
items.detail: Former PM Alexander Stubb won Finland's presidential runoff on February 11, 2024 with 51.6% against Pekka Haavisto - the narrowest margin in a Finnish runoff - and took office on March 1 for a six-year term.

items.headline: Supreme Court strikes down electoral bonds
items.detail: A five-judge Constitution bench led by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud unanimously held the electoral bonds scheme unconstitutional on February 15, 2024, saying it violated voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a). SBI was ordered to disclose donor-recipient data, which the Election Commission released in March.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils text-to-video model Sora
items.detail: OpenAI previewed Sora on February 15, 2024, an artificial intelligence model that can generate videos up to a minute long from text prompts. It was named after the Japanese word for sky.

items.headline: Ashwin becomes fastest Indian to 500 Test wickets
items.detail: Ravichandran Ashwin became the fastest Indian bowler to reach 500 Test wickets, taking the milestone on day two of the Rajkot Test against England and going past Anil Kumble's tally at the time.

items.headline: Alexei Navalny dies in Arctic prison
items.detail: Alexei Navalny, Russia's leading opposition figure and anti-corruption campaigner, died at the age of 47 in the IK-3 Arctic prison colony at Kharp weeks before Russia's presidential election.
examFacts: Place: Arctic prison colony IK-3, Kharp

items.headline: ISRO launches meteorological satellite INSAT-3DS
items.detail: ISRO launched the INSAT-3DS weather satellite on the GSLV-F14 rocket on February 17, 2024 - the first flight with the extended CUS-15 cryogenic upper stage. The 2,275 kg satellite will serve for 10 years under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

items.headline: India's biggest Test win by runs at Rajkot
items.detail: India beat England by 434 runs in the third Test at Rajkot - India's largest Test win by runs and England's heaviest defeat since 1934. Yashasvi Jaiswal hit an unbeaten 214 with 12 sixes, equalling Wasim Akram's record for sixes in a Test innings.

items.headline: First private spacecraft lands on the Moon
items.detail: Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander touched down near Malapert A crater, about 300 km from the lunar south pole, on February 22, 2024 - the first commercial spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon and the first US lunar landing since Apollo 17 in 1972. The lander tipped over to a 30-degree angle after touchdown.

items.headline: Documentary 'Dahomey' wins Berlinale Golden Bear
items.detail: Mati Diop's documentary 'Dahomey' won the Golden Bear at the 74th Berlin International Film Festival (February 15-25, 2024) - the second straight year a documentary took the top prize.

items.headline: India seal 4-1 Test series win over England
items.detail: India won the Ranchi Test by 5 wickets on February 26, 2024 to take an unassailable 3-1 lead, completing a 4-1 series win after losing the opening Test - the first such five-Test comeback in 112 years.

quiz.q: The interim Union Budget for 2024-25 was presented on:
quiz.solution: Nirmala Sitharaman presented the interim budget on February 1, 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha polls.

quiz.q: On February 15, 2024, the Supreme Court struck down which scheme as unconstitutional?
quiz.solution: A 5-judge bench led by CJI Chandrachud held it violated Article 19(1)(a) - voters' right to information.

quiz.q: Which satellite did ISRO launch on GSLV-F14 in February 2024?
quiz.solution: INSAT-3DS, a weather satellite, launched on February 17, 2024.

quiz.q: Which team won the 2024 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup?
quiz.solution: Australia beat defending champions India by 79 runs for a fourth title.

quiz.q: Taylor Swift became the first artist to win the Grammy Album of the Year award:
quiz.solution: 'Midnights' made her a four-time Album of the Year winner at the 66th Grammys.

quiz.q: Who became the fastest Indian bowler to 500 Test wickets in February 2024?
quiz.solution: Ashwin reached 500 in the Rajkot Test, going past Anil Kumble's pace.

quiz.q: India's 434-run win over England at Rajkot was notable as:
options: India's biggest Test win by runs
quiz.solution: It was India's largest Test win by runs; Jaiswal hit an unbeaten 214 with 12 sixes.

quiz.q: Alexei Navalny, who died in a prison colony in February 2024, was the leading opposition figure of:
quiz.solution: He died at 47 in the IK-3 Arctic prison colony at Kharp, weeks before Russia's election.

quiz.q: Odysseus, which landed near the Moon's south pole in February 2024, was built by:
quiz.solution: It was the first commercial spacecraft to soft-land on the Moon - the first US landing since Apollo 17.

quiz.q: How many Bharat Ratnas were announced in February 2024?
quiz.solution: Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, P.V. Narasimha Rao, Charan Singh and M.S. Swaminathan - four posthumous.

items.headline: Shehbaz Sharif sworn in as Pakistan PM again
items.detail: Shehbaz Sharif was elected Pakistan's Prime Minister for a second term on March 3-4, 2024, winning 201 votes against 92 for the PTI-backed Omar Ayub Khan - the first person to hold the premiership in two consecutive terms.
examFacts: Won 201 votes in the National Assembly

items.headline: Sweden joins NATO as its 32nd member
items.detail: Sweden formally became NATO's 32nd member on March 7, 2024, ending about 200 years of military non-alignment, after Hungary became the last member to ratify its accession.

items.headline: Election Commissioner Arun Goel resigns
items.detail: Election Commissioner Arun Goel resigned on March 9, 2024, days before the announcement of the Lok Sabha election schedule, leaving the Election Commission with only Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
examFacts: Resigned ahead of the 2024 general election

items.headline: Miss World pageant held in Mumbai
items.detail: The 71st Miss World pageant was held at the Jio World Convention Centre, Mumbai on March 9, 2024 - India hosting it for the second time after 1996. Krystyna Pyszkova of the Czech Republic won, with Lebanon's Yasmina Zaytoun runner-up.

items.headline: Oscars 2024: 'Oppenheimer' dominates with 7 awards
items.detail: Christopher Nolan's 'Oppenheimer' won 7 Oscars including Best Picture at the 96th Academy Awards on March 10, 2024. Cillian Murphy won Best Actor, Emma Stone Best Actress, and Robert Downey Jr. Best Supporting Actor.

items.headline: Centre notifies CAA rules
items.detail: The Union government notified the rules for implementing the Citizenship Amendment Act on March 11, 2024, enabling citizenship for persecuted minorities of six communities from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh who entered India before 2015.
examFacts: Covers migrants from Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh

items.headline: Mission Divyastra: Agni-5 tested with MIRV technology
items.detail: India test-fired Agni-5 with Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle (MIRV) technology under 'Mission Divyastra' on March 11, 2024, one missile carrying several warheads that can hit separate targets.

items.headline: SBI discloses electoral bonds data
items.detail: After the Supreme Court rejected its plea to delay disclosure till June 30, the State Bank of India submitted electoral bonds data to the Election Commission on March 12, 2024; the poll panel published it on March 14.

items.headline: EU Parliament adopts world's first AI law
items.detail: The European Parliament adopted the EU Artificial Intelligence Act on March 13, 2024 - the world's first comprehensive AI law, using a risk-based approach that bans unacceptable-risk uses like social scoring. It entered into force on August 1, 2024.

items.headline: Putin re-elected with record 88% in Russia
items.detail: Vladimir Putin won the March 15-17, 2024 Russian presidential election with a record 88.48% of votes, securing a fifth term, the highest share for any presidential winner in post-Soviet Russia.

items.headline: Lok Sabha election schedule announced
items.detail: Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar announced the schedule for the 18th Lok Sabha election on March 16, 2024 - a seven-phase poll from April 19 to June 1, with counting on June 4.

items.headline: Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal arrested
items.detail: Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on March 21, 2024 in connection with the Delhi excise policy money-laundering case - the first sitting CM arrested while in office.

items.headline: Deadly concert hall attack near Moscow
items.detail: Gunmen attacked the Crocus City Hall concert venue near Moscow on March 22, 2024, killing 151 people - Russia's deadliest attack since the 2004 Beslan siege. The Islamic State's Khorasan branch (ISIS-K) was blamed.

items.headline: IPL 2024 season begins
items.detail: The IPL 2024 season opened on March 22, 2024 with Chennai Super Kings beating Royal Challengers Bengaluru by 6 wickets at the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai. The season had 74 matches, with the final also in Chennai on May 26.
examFacts: Opening match: CSK beat RCB by 6 wickets

items.headline: Sonam Wangchuk ends 21-day hunger strike for Ladakh
items.detail: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 21-day hunger strike on March 26, 2024, which had demanded statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule.
examFacts: Demands: statehood, Sixth Schedule for Ladakh

quiz.q: In March 2024, the Union government notified rules for implementing which law?
quiz.solution: CAA implementation rules were notified on March 11, 2024.

quiz.q: Which institution disclosed electoral bonds data in March 2024 after the Supreme Court rejected its delay plea?
quiz.solution: SBI submitted the data on March 12, 2024; the ECI published it on March 14.

quiz.q: Who won Best Picture at the 96th Academy Awards (March 2024)?
quiz.solution: 'Oppenheimer' won 7 Oscars including Best Picture; Cillian Murphy won Best Actor.

quiz.q: Sweden became NATO's 32nd member in March 2024, ending about 200 years of:
quiz.solution: Sweden formally joined NATO on March 7, 2024.

quiz.q: India's 'Mission Divyastra' in March 2024 tested which capability on the Agni-5 missile?
quiz.solution: Agni-5 flew with MIRV technology, one missile carrying several independently targetable warheads.

quiz.q: Who was elected Pakistan's Prime Minister for a second term in March 2024?
quiz.solution: Shehbaz Sharif won 201 votes in the National Assembly for a second consecutive term.

quiz.q: Vladimir Putin won the March 2024 Russian presidential election with a record vote share of:
quiz.solution: Putin won 88.48% - the highest for any presidential winner in post-Soviet Russia - for a fifth term.

quiz.q: The March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack near Moscow, killing 151, was blamed on:
quiz.solution: The Islamic State's Khorasan branch was blamed for Russia's deadliest attack since Beslan 2004.

quiz.q: Krystyna Pyszkova, who won the Miss World pageant in Mumbai in March 2024, represented:
quiz.solution: The Czech model won; Lebanon's Yasmina Zaytoun was runner-up.

quiz.q: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act, adopted by Parliament in March 2024, is notable as:
options: The EU's first data privacy law
The world's first comprehensive AI law
A ban on all AI research
quiz.solution: It is a risk-based law - the world's first comprehensive AI regulation - in force from August 1, 2024.

items.headline: Indonesia's Mount Ruang erupts twice
items.detail: Mount Ruang in Indonesia's North Sulawesi erupted for a second time in April 2024, forcing the evacuation of more than 12,000 people.

items.headline: Israeli strike hits Iranian consulate in Damascus
items.detail: An Israeli air strike destroyed Iran's consulate annex in Damascus on April 1, 2024, killing 16 people including senior Quds Force commander Brig. Gen. Mohammad Reza Zahedi, prompting Iran to vow retaliation.

items.headline: Mexico cuts diplomatic ties with Ecuador
items.detail: Mexico severed diplomatic relations with Ecuador after Ecuadorian police raided the Mexican embassy in Quito to arrest former Vice President Jorge Glas, a breach of the Vienna Convention.
examFacts: Cause: raid on Mexican embassy in Quito

items.headline: Zimbabwe launches gold-backed currency
items.detail: Zimbabwe's central bank launched 'Zimbabwe Gold' (ZiG), a new currency backed by gold reserves and foreign currencies, to replace the collapsing Zimbabwe dollar.
examFacts: Backed by gold and forex reserves

items.headline: Total solar eclipse sweeps North America
items.detail: A total solar eclipse - the 'Great North American Eclipse' - crossed Mexico, the United States and Canada on April 8, 2024, with maximum totality of 4 minutes 28 seconds over Mexico.

items.headline: Iran launches first-ever direct attack on Israel
items.detail: Iran launched Operation True Promise against Israel on the night of April 13-14, 2024 - its first direct attack - firing over 300 drones and missiles. Israel and its allies intercepted about 99%, with the Arrow-3 system and a first combat use of the US SM-3 missile.
examFacts: Iran's first direct attack on Israel
Systems: Arrow-3, Iron Dome, US SM-3

items.headline: Olympic flame lit at Olympia for Paris 2024
items.detail: The Paris 2024 Olympic flame was lit at Ancient Olympia, Greece on April 16, 2024, beginning a relay across Greece and then France aboard the three-masted Belem, arriving in Marseille on May 9.
examFacts: Flame sailed to Marseille on the Belem

items.headline: 18th Lok Sabha election begins in seven phases
items.detail: Voting for the 18th Lok Sabha began on April 19, 2024 - the world's largest election, with 969 million eligible voters - held in seven phases till June 1, 2024 across 543 constituencies, with results on June 4.

items.headline: Israel retaliates with strikes near Isfahan
items.detail: Israel carried out limited strikes on Iranian military sites near Isfahan on April 18-19, 2024, in retaliation for Iran's drone and missile attack, keeping the exchange calibrated.
examFacts: Target: Iranian military sites near Isfahan

items.headline: UK's Rwanda asylum law gets royal assent
items.detail: The Safety of Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act received royal assent on April 25, 2024, declaring Rwanda a safe country for relocated asylum seekers. No one was ever sent to Rwanda under it, and it was repealed in 2025.

items.headline: Vietnam's parliament chairman resigns amid probe
items.detail: Vuong Dinh Hue, Chairman of Vietnam's National Assembly, resigned on April 26, 2024 amid a sweeping anti-corruption campaign in the country.

items.headline: China to host Hamas-Fatah unity talks
items.detail: China announced it would host reconciliation talks between Palestinian factions Hamas and Fatah, part of Beijing's push for a role in Middle East diplomacy.

items.headline: Shenzhou-17 crew returns from Tiangong
items.detail: The Shenzhou-17 crew returned to Earth on April 30, 2024 after about six months aboard China's Tiangong space station.

items.headline: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao sentenced
items.detail: Changpeng Zhao, founder of crypto exchange Binance, was sentenced to four months in prison in the US for money-laundering violations linked to the exchange.

items.headline: Kenya floods kill nearly 170
items.detail: Flooding in Kenya pushed the death toll to 169 with 91 people missing, amid devastating rains across East Africa.

quiz.q: The 2024 Lok Sabha election was held in how many phases?
quiz.solution: Voting ran in seven phases from April 19 to June 1, 2024, with 969 million eligible voters.

quiz.q: The 'Great North American Eclipse' of April 8, 2024 reached maximum totality over:
quiz.solution: Maximum totality of 4 minutes 28 seconds occurred near Nazas, Durango, Mexico.

quiz.q: Iran's April 2024 direct attack on Israel was launched in retaliation for:
options: The killing of Hamas chief in Qatar
A strike on its consulate in Damascus
quiz.solution: An April 1 Israeli strike on Iran's Damascus consulate annex killed Quds Force commander Zahedi.

quiz.q: What was Operation True Promise?
options: Iran's first direct drone and missile attack on Israel
quiz.solution: Iran launched over 300 drones and missiles at Israel on April 13-14, 2024; about 99% were intercepted.

quiz.q: The UK's Rwanda (Asylum and Immigration) Act, which got royal assent in April 2024, declared:
options: Rwanda a safe country for asylum seekers
A new visa scheme for students
quiz.solution: It declared Rwanda safe for relocated asylum seekers; it never came into force and was repealed in 2025.

quiz.q: The Olympic flame for Paris 2024 was lit at:
quiz.solution: It was lit at Ancient Olympia on April 16, 2024 and sailed to Marseille aboard the Belem.

quiz.q: Mexico severed ties with Ecuador in April 2024 after Ecuador raided which building?
quiz.solution: Ecuadorian police entered the Mexican embassy to arrest former Vice President Jorge Glas.

quiz.q: Zimbabwe's new currency launched in April 2024, backed by gold reserves, is called:
quiz.solution: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe launched the gold-backed ZiG to replace the collapsing dollar.

quiz.q: The Shenzhou-17 crew that returned in April 2024 had spent six months aboard:
quiz.solution: China's Shenzhou-17 crew returned from the Tiangong space station on April 30, 2024.

quiz.q: Changpeng Zhao, sentenced in the US in April 2024, founded which crypto exchange?
quiz.solution: The Binance founder got four months for money-laundering violations.

items.headline: Air India Express cancels 85+ flights amid staff protest
items.detail: Air India Express cancelled over 85 flights after large numbers of cabin crew reported sick in protest over working conditions under the Tata group, disrupting air travel for two days.

items.headline: Supreme Court grants interim bail to Arvind Kejriwal
items.detail: The Supreme Court granted Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal interim bail in the liquor policy money-laundering case on May 10, 2024, allowing him to campaign in the general election.

items.headline: Strongest solar storm in decades sparks global auroras
items.detail: A G5 'extreme' geomagnetic storm - the strongest to hit Earth since 1989 - struck on May 10-11, 2024 after multiple X-class solar flares, making auroras visible as far south as Florida and in northern India.
examFacts: Auroras seen at unusually low latitudes

items.headline: Twelve Maoists killed in Chhattisgarh encounter
items.detail: Security forces killed 12 Maoists in an encounter in Chhattisgarh on May 10, 2024, one of the biggest operations of the year against left-wing extremism.

items.headline: Assembly elections held in Odisha and Andhra Pradesh
items.detail: Assembly elections were held alongside the Lok Sabha polls - in Andhra Pradesh on May 13, 2024, and in Odisha in four phases from May 13 to June 1, 2024.

items.headline: Cannes 2024: 'Anora' wins Palme d'Or
items.detail: Sean Baker's 'Anora' won the Palme d'Or at the 77th Cannes Film Festival (May 14-25, 2024), with Greta Gerwig heading the jury. The film later won the 2025 Oscar for Best Picture.

items.headline: Lawrence Wong becomes Singapore's Prime Minister
items.detail: Lawrence Wong was sworn in as Singapore's fourth Prime Minister on May 15, 2024, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong. He is the first PM born after Singapore's 1965 independence.

items.headline: Iran President Raisi dies in helicopter crash
items.detail: Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi, Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian and six others died when their helicopter crashed in fog near Varzaqan, East Azerbaijan province on May 19, 2024. First Vice President Mohammad Mokhber became acting president, and a snap election was held on June 28, 2024.
examFacts: Killed: President Raisi and Foreign Minister

items.headline: India observes state mourning for Raisi
items.detail: India declared one day of state mourning on May 21, 2024 following the death of Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi.

items.headline: Charges framed against ex-WFI chief Brij Bhushan Singh
items.detail: Sexual harassment charges were framed in a Delhi court against former Wrestling Federation of India president and BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on May 21, 2024, months after a protest by top women wrestlers.

items.headline: Calcutta HC cancels OBC certificates issued since 2010
items.detail: The Calcutta High Court invalidated all OBC certificates issued by the West Bengal government since 2010, a major order in the state's reservation policy.

items.headline: Cyclone Remal batters Bengal and Bangladesh coasts
items.detail: Cyclone Remal made landfall on the Bangladesh coast near Mongla on May 26, 2024 as a severe cyclonic storm, also hitting West Bengal and Northeast India. It killed over 60 people, forced the closure of Kolkata airport and left millions affected.
examFacts: Areas: Bangladesh, West Bengal, Northeast India

items.headline: KKR win their third IPL title
items.detail: Kolkata Knight Riders beat Sunrisers Hyderabad by 8 wickets in the IPL 2024 final in Chennai on May 26, 2024 to win their third title. Virat Kohli won the Orange Cap with 741 runs.
examFacts: Final: KKR beat SRH by 8 wickets

items.headline: Delhi logs 52.3 degrees Celsius, an all-time record
items.detail: The IMD recorded 52.3 degrees Celsius at Delhi's Mungeshpur weather station on May 29, 2024 - the highest temperature ever recorded in the capital - amid a severe heatwave across north India.

items.headline: ANC loses majority in South Africa election
items.detail: South Africa's ANC, in power since 1994, lost its parliamentary majority in the May 29, 2024 election, winning 40% of the vote and 159 seats. It formed a Government of National Unity with the DA and others, and Cyril Ramaphosa was re-elected president.
examFacts: New coalition: Government of National Unity

quiz.q: Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi, who died in a May 2024 helicopter crash, was also Iran's:
quiz.solution: Raisi was Iran's President; he died with Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian in the May 19, 2024 crash.

quiz.q: Which film won the Palme d'Or at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival?
quiz.solution: Sean Baker's 'Anora' won the Palme d'Or; it later won the 2025 Best Picture Oscar.

quiz.q: Which team won the IPL 2024 title?
quiz.solution: KKR beat Sunrisers Hyderabad by 8 wickets to win their third title.

quiz.q: Lawrence Wong became the Prime Minister of which country in May 2024?
quiz.solution: He became Singapore's fourth PM on May 15, 2024, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong.

quiz.q: Delhi's highest-ever recorded temperature of 52.3 degrees Celsius was logged at:
quiz.solution: The IMD recorded 52.3 C at Mungeshpur on May 29, 2024.

quiz.q: Cyclone Remal, which struck in May 2024, formed in which sea?
quiz.solution: Remal formed in the Bay of Bengal and hit the Bangladesh-West Bengal coast on May 26, 2024.

quiz.q: In the May 2024 election, which party lost its majority in South Africa for the first time since 1994?
quiz.solution: The ANC fell to about 40% and formed a Government of National Unity with the DA and others.

quiz.q: The May 2024 G5 geomagnetic storm, the strongest since 1989, produced which phenomenon?
quiz.solution: Auroras were seen as far south as Florida and in northern India after multiple X-class flares.

quiz.q: Why did the Supreme Court grant interim bail to Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal in May 2024?
options: To campaign in the general election
quiz.solution: The May 10, 2024 interim bail in the excise policy case allowed him to campaign.

quiz.q: Who won the Orange Cap for most runs (741) in IPL 2024?
quiz.solution: Virat Kohli of RCB topped the run charts with 741 runs.

items.headline: Claudia Sheinbaum elected Mexico's first woman president
items.detail: Claudia Sheinbaum of the ruling MORENA party won Mexico's presidential election on June 2, 2024 with about 61% of the vote, becoming the country's first woman and first person of Jewish descent to be elected president.

items.headline: Lok Sabha election results: NDA wins 293 seats
items.detail: Results of the 18th Lok Sabha election were declared on June 4, 2024. The BJP-led NDA won 293 seats and the INDIA bloc 234. The BJP alone won 240 (down from 303 in 2019) and the Congress 99, making it a coalition government for Modi's third term.

items.headline: NEET-UG 2024 row: NTA chief dismissed
items.detail: The NEET-UG 2024 result row erupted after results were announced early amid allegations of irregularities and paper leaks. NTA Director General Subodh Kumar Singh was dismissed on June 22, 2024, and a high-powered committee was formed to reform the examination body.
examFacts: NTA DG Subodh Kumar Singh dismissed

items.headline: World Environment Day 2024
items.detail: World Environment Day was observed on June 5, 2024 with the theme 'Land restoration, desertification and drought resilience', hosted by Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

items.headline: Boeing Starliner flies astronauts to ISS
items.detail: Boeing's Starliner capsule launched its first crewed test flight on June 5, 2024, carrying Butch Wilmore and Sunita Williams to the ISS. Thruster problems later ruled out a Starliner return, and the pair came back only in March 2025 on a SpaceX Crew Dragon.

items.headline: European Parliament elections see right-wing gains
items.detail: Elections to the 720-seat European Parliament were held on June 6-9, 2024. The centre-right EPP led by Ursula von der Leyen won the most seats (188), while right-wing groups like Patriots for Europe made gains; von der Leyen retained the Commission presidency.

items.headline: Modi sworn in as Prime Minister for a third term
items.detail: Narendra Modi took oath as Prime Minister on June 9, 2024 for a third consecutive term, leading a coalition government for the first time, with the TDP and JD(U) as key allies.

items.headline: Alcaraz and Swiatek win French Open titles
items.detail: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev for the men's singles title and Iga Swiatek defeated Jasmine Paolini to win a third straight French Open at Roland Garros (May 26 to June 9, 2024).

items.headline: BJP ends Naveen Patnaik's 24-year rule in Odisha
items.detail: The BJP won 79 of 147 seats in the Odisha assembly election, and Mohan Charan Majhi was sworn in as the 15th Chief Minister on June 12, 2024 - the first CM from the Santal tribal community, succeeding Naveen Patnaik (in office since 2000).

items.headline: Chandrababu Naidu takes oath as Andhra Pradesh CM
items.detail: TDP chief N. Chandrababu Naidu was sworn in as Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister on June 12, 2024, a record fourth term in the office, succeeding Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy.
examFacts: Fourth term as CM - a record

items.headline: 50th G7 summit held in Apulia, Italy
items.detail: The 50th G7 summit was held at Borgo Egnazia, Fasano in Apulia, Italy from June 13-15, 2024, chaired by PM Giorgia Meloni. PM Narendra Modi was among invited outreach leaders, and Pope Francis became the first pope to address a G7 summit.
examFacts: First pope to attend a G7 summit

items.headline: 18th Lok Sabha constituted
items.detail: The 17th Lok Sabha was dissolved on June 5 and the 18th Lok Sabha was constituted on June 24, 2024, with President Droupadi Murmu addressing the new House on June 27.

items.headline: China's Chang'e-6 returns first far-side Moon samples
items.detail: China's Chang'e-6 probe returned to Earth on June 25, 2024 with about 1,935 grams of material from the far side of the Moon - the first samples ever collected from that hemisphere.

items.headline: Om Birla re-elected Lok Sabha Speaker
items.detail: Om Birla was re-elected Speaker of the Lok Sabha on June 26, 2024 for a second consecutive term, defeating the INDIA bloc's K. Suresh in a voice vote.

items.headline: India win T20 World Cup, ending 11-year ICC title drought
items.detail: India beat South Africa by 7 runs in the final at Kensington Oval, Barbados on June 29, 2024 to win their second ICC Men's T20 World Cup - becoming the first team to win the tournament undefeated. Jasprit Bumrah was Player of the Tournament.
examFacts: Final: India beat South Africa by 7 runs
Player of the Tournament: Jasprit Bumrah

quiz.q: Who became Mexico's first woman president in the June 2024 election?
quiz.solution: Claudia Sheinbaum of MORENA won with about 61% of the vote.

quiz.q: How many seats did the BJP win in the 2024 Lok Sabha election?
quiz.solution: The BJP won 240 seats (down from 303 in 2019); its NDA alliance won 293.

quiz.q: India beat which team by 7 runs to win the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
quiz.solution: India beat South Africa by 7 runs in the Barbados final on June 29, 2024.

quiz.q: Who was named Player of the Tournament at the 2024 T20 World Cup?
quiz.solution: Jasprit Bumrah was Player of the Tournament as India won the title unbeaten.

quiz.q: Who was sworn in as Odisha's 15th Chief Minister in June 2024?
quiz.solution: BJP's Mohan Charan Majhi took oath on June 12, 2024, ending Naveen Patnaik's 24-year rule.

quiz.q: N. Chandrababu Naidu became Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister for which record term in June 2024?
quiz.solution: The TDP chief took oath on June 12, 2024 for a record fourth term.

quiz.q: The 50th G7 summit in June 2024 was hosted by which country?
quiz.solution: Italy hosted the summit at Borgo Egnazia, Apulia from June 13-15, 2024.

quiz.q: Om Birla was re-elected Speaker of the Lok Sabha in June 2024 for which term?
quiz.solution: He won a second consecutive term on June 26, 2024.

quiz.q: China's Chang'e-6 mission, which returned in June 2024, collected the first samples from:
options: The far side of the Moon
quiz.solution: It brought back about 1,935 grams from the far side, a first in lunar exploration.

quiz.q: The theme of World Environment Day 2024 was:
options: Land restoration, desertification and drought resilience
quiz.solution: The June 5 event, hosted by Riyadh, focused on land restoration and drought resilience.

items.headline: Economic Survey 2023-24 tabled before the Budget
items.detail: The Economic Survey, the Finance Ministry's review of the economy prepared under Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran, was presented in Parliament a day before the Union Budget, as is the annual practice.
examFacts: Prepared under CEA: V. Anantha Nageswaran

items.headline: New criminal codes come into force
items.detail: Three new criminal laws - the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam - took effect on July 1, 2024, replacing the colonial-era Indian Penal Code (1860), Code of Criminal Procedure (1898) and Indian Evidence Act (1872).

items.headline: NATO holds 75th anniversary summit in Washington
items.detail: NATO's 75th anniversary summit was held in Washington DC from July 9-11, 2024, themed 'Ukraine and transatlantic security'. The 32 members pledged long-term support for Ukraine, and it was the first summit with Sweden as a member.
examFacts: First summit with Sweden as member

items.headline: Spain win Euro 2024
items.detail: Spain beat England 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final at Berlin on July 14, 2024 to win a record fourth European title, winning all seven matches. Rodri was Player of the Tournament.

items.headline: Alcaraz and Krejcikova win Wimbledon singles
items.detail: Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic to retain the men's title, and Barbora Krejcikova of the Czech Republic beat Jasmine Paolini of Italy for the women's title at the 137th Wimbledon Championships.

items.headline: WazirX loses $234 million in cyberattack
items.detail: Indian cryptocurrency exchange WazirX announced a hack in which about USD 234 million was stolen, roughly half the platform's assets.

items.headline: Global IT outage hits Windows systems
items.detail: A faulty CrowdStrike software update crashed millions of Windows computers worldwide with 'blue screen of death' errors, grounding flights and disrupting hospitals, banks and broadcasters.

items.headline: Vietnam's top leader Nguyen Phu Trong dies
items.detail: Nguyen Phu Trong, General Secretary of Vietnam's Communist Party, died at the age of 80. President To Lam took over the post on an acting basis.
examFacts: Role: Communist Party General Secretary of Vietnam

items.headline: ICJ declares Israel's occupation unlawful
items.detail: The International Court of Justice ruled that Israel's settlement construction and annexation in the West Bank and East Jerusalem were unlawful, and said its presence in the occupied Palestinian territory was illegal.
examFacts: Ruling on West Bank and East Jerusalem

items.headline: US journalist Gershkovich sentenced in Russia
items.detail: A Russian court convicted Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich of spying and sentenced him to 16 years in prison. He was freed less than a month later in the largest East-West prisoner swap since the Cold War.
examFacts: Freed in the August 1, 2024 prisoner swap

items.headline: Joe Biden withdraws from US presidential race
items.detail: US President Joe Biden withdrew from the 2024 presidential race on July 21, 2024, endorsing Vice President Kamala Harris, who became the Democratic nominee the next day.

items.headline: Union Budget 2024-25 presented
items.detail: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2024-25 on July 23, 2024, the first budget of the NDA government's third term. The fiscal deficit target was set at 4.9% of GDP, the standard deduction was raised to Rs 75,000, the angel tax was abolished, and capital gains were rationalised (STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5%).

items.headline: Moidams of Assam join UNESCO World Heritage list
items.detail: The Charaideo Moidam tomb complex in Assam, the mound-burial system of the Ahom dynasty, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, announced on July 26, 2024.

items.headline: India and China agree to push border disengagement
items.detail: India and China agreed to cooperate on pulling troops back from their disputed border, with the aim of achieving complete disengagement as quickly as possible.
examFacts: Focus: troop disengagement at the border

items.headline: Kargil Vijay Diwas observed
items.detail: Kargil Vijay Diwas was observed on July 26, marking the anniversary of India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War under Operation Vijay, which ended on July 26, 1999.

items.headline: Paris Olympics open
items.detail: The 2024 Summer Olympics opened in Paris on July 26, 2024 with the motto 'Games Wide Open' and mascot 'Phryges'. About 10,700 athletes from 204 nations competed; the United States topped the medal table.

items.headline: Venezuela election result disputed
items.detail: Venezuela's election authority declared President Nicolas Maduro the winner of the July 28, 2024 election with about 52% against opposition candidate Edmundo Gonzalez's 43%, a result the opposition and many countries rejected.

items.headline: Wayanad landslides kill over 400
items.detail: Multiple landslides hit Mundakkai and Chooralmala villages in Wayanad district, Kerala on July 30, 2024, killing 420 people - the deadliest disaster in Kerala's history - and destroying the Chooralmala bridge.

quiz.q: Who presented the Union Budget 2024-25 in Parliament on July 23, 2024?
quiz.solution: It was the first budget of the NDA government's third term, presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

quiz.q: The fiscal deficit target in the Union Budget 2024-25 was set at:
quiz.solution: The Budget 2024-25 set the fiscal deficit target at 4.9% of GDP.

quiz.q: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, effective July 1, 2024, replaced which colonial-era law?
quiz.solution: The BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860; the CrPC and Evidence Act were replaced by the other two Sanhitas.

quiz.q: The July 2024 landslides at Mundakkai and Chooralmala occurred in which district?
quiz.solution: The Wayanad landslides of July 30, 2024 killed 420 people, Kerala's deadliest disaster.

quiz.q: Which Indian site was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2024?
quiz.solution: The Ahom-era burial mounds at Charaideo in Assam joined the UNESCO list.

quiz.q: Which country won UEFA Euro 2024, its record fourth title?
quiz.solution: Spain beat England 2-1 in the Berlin final, winning all seven matches.

quiz.q: Who won the men's singles title at Wimbledon 2024?
quiz.solution: Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic in the final to retain his title.

quiz.q: The 2024 NATO summit marking the alliance's 75th anniversary was held in:
quiz.solution: NATO's 75th anniversary summit was held in Washington DC from July 9-11, 2024.

quiz.q: The global IT outage of July 19, 2024 was caused by a faulty update from:
quiz.solution: A faulty CrowdStrike update crashed Windows systems worldwide.

quiz.q: India's victory in the Kargil War (1999) is commemorated by which operation's name?
quiz.solution: The Kargil War ended on July 26, 1999, celebrated annually as Kargil Vijay Diwas.

items.headline: Manu Bhaker wins two bronze medals at one Olympics
items.detail: Shooter Manu Bhaker won bronze in the women's 10m air pistol and then in the 10m air pistol mixed team with Sarabjot Singh, becoming the first Indian since independence to win two medals at a single Games and India's first woman shooter to win an Olympic medal.
examFacts: Two bronze: 10m air pistol + mixed team
First Indian post-independence with two medals at one Games

items.headline: India finish Paris Olympics with 6 medals
items.detail: India ended the Paris 2024 Olympics (July 26 to August 11) with 6 medals - one silver and five bronze - ranking 71st, its second-best haul after Tokyo.

items.headline: India-China hold 30th round of border talks
items.detail: India and China held the 30th round of border talks in New Delhi on August 1, 2024, agreeing to speed up negotiations and keep border areas peaceful.

items.headline: Swapnil Kusale wins shooting bronze
items.detail: Swapnil Kusale won bronze in the men's 50m rifle three positions at the Paris Olympics, India's seventh Olympic shooting medal overall.

items.headline: Largest East-West prisoner swap since the Cold War
items.detail: Russia and the West carried out their biggest prisoner exchange since the Cold War on August 1, 2024, freeing US journalist Evan Gershkovich, Paul Whelan and opposition figure Vladimir Kara-Murza in a 24-person, multi-country swap.
examFacts: Largest swap since the Cold War

items.headline: Famine confirmed in Sudan's Darfur
items.detail: The IPC Famine Review Committee confirmed famine in the Zamzam camp in Sudan's North Darfur, the first famine classification since 2017, amid the country's civil war.

items.headline: Israel confirms killing of Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif
items.detail: Israel confirmed it killed Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif in a July 13 air strike in Khan Younis, Gaza. Deif was the long-time commander of the al-Qassam Brigades.

items.headline: Katie Ledecky wins 13th Olympic medal
items.detail: American swimmer Katie Ledecky won her 13th Olympic medal at the Paris Games, becoming the most decorated US woman in Olympic history.
examFacts: 13th Olympic medal - most by a US woman

items.headline: Sheikh Hasina resigns; Yunus heads Bangladesh interim government
items.detail: Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina resigned on August 5, 2024 amid mass student-led protests and fled to India, ending her 15-year rule. Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus was sworn in as chief adviser of the interim government on August 8, 2024.
examFacts: Interim chief adviser: Muhammad Yunus (sworn in August 8)

items.headline: Nikkei suffers worst day since 1987
items.detail: Japan's Nikkei 225 index crashed more than 12% on August 5, 2024, its biggest daily fall since Black Monday of 1987, triggering steep losses across global markets.

items.headline: US court rules Google maintained illegal search monopoly
items.detail: A US federal judge ruled in United States v. Google that the company violated the Sherman Antitrust Act by illegally maintaining a monopoly in internet search.

items.headline: Duplantis breaks pole vault world record for gold
items.detail: Sweden's Armand 'Mondo' Duplantis won back-to-back Olympic pole vault titles at Paris 2024, clearing a world record 6.25 m.

items.headline: Vinesh Phogat disqualified from Olympic final
items.detail: Vinesh Phogat was disqualified from the women's 50 kg wrestling final at the Paris Olympics after failing the morning weigh-in, having reached the final by beating unbeaten champion Yui Susaki. She announced immediate retirement; her CAS appeal for a joint silver was dismissed.

items.headline: Neeraj Chopra wins silver at Paris Olympics
items.detail: Neeraj Chopra won silver in the men's javelin throw at the Paris Olympics with 89.45 m, becoming the first Indian individual athlete to hold both an Olympic gold and silver.
examFacts: First Indian individual athlete with Olympic gold and silver

items.headline: India men's hockey team wins back-to-back Olympic bronze
items.detail: The Indian men's hockey team beat Spain in the bronze-medal match at the Paris Olympics, winning a second consecutive Olympic bronze. Harmanpreet Singh was captain.

items.headline: Aman Sehrawat becomes youngest Indian Olympic medallist
items.detail: Wrestler Aman Sehrawat won bronze in the men's freestyle 57 kg event at the Paris Olympics, becoming the youngest-ever Indian Olympic medallist at 21.

items.headline: Doctor's rape-murder at R.G. Kar Hospital sparks protests
items.detail: A 31-year-old post-graduate trainee doctor was raped and murdered at R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on August 9, 2024, triggering nationwide protests by doctors and demands for safer workplaces for women.
examFacts: Location: R.G. Kar Medical College, Kolkata

items.headline: India celebrates 78th Independence Day
items.detail: India celebrated its 78th Independence Day on August 15, 2024, with the Prime Minister hoisting the tricolour and addressing the nation from the Red Fort, Delhi.

items.headline: Gaza death toll crosses 40,000
items.detail: Gaza's health ministry reported that more than 40,000 Palestinians had been killed in the Israel-Hamas war, including over 16,000 children.

items.headline: Sweden records first case of new mpox variant outside Africa
items.detail: Sweden confirmed the first case of the new mpox clade I variant outside Africa, days after the WHO declared the outbreak a public health emergency.
examFacts: First case of clade I outside Africa: Sweden

items.headline: Largest single Russian surrender of the war
items.detail: Ukraine's security service said 102 Russian soldiers were captured in the Kursk region, the largest single group surrender of Russian troops since the war began.

items.headline: ISRO launches EOS-08 on SSLV's final development flight
items.detail: ISRO launched the EOS-08 Earth observation satellite aboard the SSLV-D3 on August 16, 2024 - the third and final development flight of the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle. The 175.5 kg satellite carries day-night imaging and disaster-monitoring payloads.
examFacts: Launch: SSLV-D3, third and final development flight

items.headline: PM Modi makes first Indian PM visit to Ukraine
items.detail: PM Narendra Modi visited Kyiv on August 23, 2024 - the first visit to Ukraine by an Indian Prime Minister - urging President Zelenskyy to end the war and offering India's mediation.
examFacts: First Indian PM visit to Ukraine

items.headline: Paris Paralympics open
items.detail: The 2024 Summer Paralympics opened in Paris on August 28, 2024 - the city's first Paralympics - with about 4,400 athletes from 170 nations and mascot 'The Phryges'. China topped the medal table.

quiz.q: How many medals did India win at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
quiz.solution: India won 6 medals - 1 silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 bronze - ranking 71st.

quiz.q: Which Indian became the first since independence to win two medals at a single Olympic Games?
quiz.solution: Manu Bhaker won bronze in the 10m air pistol and the mixed team event at Paris 2024.

quiz.q: Neeraj Chopra's silver-medal javelin throw at the Paris Olympics measured:
quiz.solution: He threw 89.45 m for silver, becoming the first Indian individual athlete with both Olympic gold and silver.

quiz.q: Sheikh Hasina, who resigned as Bangladesh PM in August 2024, fled to which country?
quiz.solution: She resigned on August 5, 2024 amid mass protests and fled to India.

quiz.q: Who was sworn in as chief adviser of Bangladesh's interim government in August 2024?
quiz.solution: Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus took oath on August 8, 2024.

quiz.q: Which launch vehicle carried ISRO's EOS-08 satellite in August 2024?
quiz.solution: EOS-08 flew on the SSLV-D3, the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle's third and final development flight.

quiz.q: Vinesh Phogat was disqualified from the Paris Olympics wrestling final for:
quiz.solution: She failed the morning weigh-in in the women's 50 kg category; her CAS appeal was later dismissed.

quiz.q: The Nikkei index crash of August 5, 2024 was Japan's biggest daily fall since:
quiz.solution: The Nikkei fell over 12%, its worst day since Black Monday in October 1987.

quiz.q: In August 2024, a US court held that Google violated which law by maintaining a search monopoly?
quiz.solution: The court ruled Google violated the Sherman Antitrust Act in the search-monopoly case.

quiz.q: PM Modi's August 2024 visit to Kyiv was the first by an Indian PM to which country?
quiz.solution: He visited Kyiv on August 23, 2024, the first Indian PM visit to Ukraine, urging peace talks.

items.headline: India's first paperless election held in Madhya Pradesh
items.detail: Madhya Pradesh conducted India's first paperless election, a pilot for a Sarpanch post in Ratua Ratanpur village in Berasia tehsil, Bhopal, recording 84% turnout.

items.headline: Jordan first country verified for eliminating leprosy
items.detail: Jordan became the first country in the world to receive WHO verification for eliminating leprosy, with no locally transmitted cases for over two decades.

items.headline: Algeria's Tebboune re-elected President
items.detail: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune won a second term with about 94.7% of the votes.

items.headline: RBI allows OCI cardholders education loans under LRS
items.detail: The RBI clarified that resident OCI cardholders are eligible for education loans to study abroad, with remittances capped at USD 250,000 per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.

items.headline: India's best-ever Paralympics: 29 medals
items.detail: India won 29 medals - 7 gold, 9 silver and 13 bronze - at the Paris Paralympics (August 28 to September 8, 2024), its best-ever tally, finishing 18th. Navdeep Singh won javelin gold, Harvinder Singh took India's first Paralympic archery gold, and Sheetal Devi became the youngest Indian Paralympic medallist.

items.headline: Odisha launches CM-KISAN scheme for farmers
items.detail: Odisha CM Mohan Charan Majhi launched the CM-KISAN Yojana on Nuakhai festival, replacing the KALIA scheme. Small farmers will get Rs 4,000 a year.

items.headline: International Literacy Day 2024 observed
items.detail: International Literacy Day was observed on September 8, 2024 with the theme 'Promoting Multilingual Education: Literacy for Mutual Understanding and Peace'.

items.headline: US Open 2024: Sinner and Sabalenka win singles
items.detail: Italy's Jannik Sinner beat Taylor Fritz to win the men's singles, while Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka beat Jessica Pegula for the women's title at the US Open in New York.

items.headline: Tuhin Kanta Pandey appointed Finance Secretary
items.detail: IAS officer Tuhin Kanta Pandey was appointed Finance Secretary, replacing T V Somanathan, who took over as Cabinet Secretary.

items.headline: India test-fires Agni-4 ballistic missile
items.detail: India successfully test-fired the nuclear-capable Agni-4 intermediate-range ballistic missile from the ITR at Chandipur, Odisha. Its range is about 4,000 km.

items.headline: SEMICON India 2024 inaugurated
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2024 at Greater Noida with the theme 'Shaping the Semiconductor Future', showcasing India's semiconductor ambitions.

items.headline: China launches 10 more Geespace satellites
items.detail: China launched the third batch of 10 Geespace low Earth orbit satellites from Taiyuan, part of a planned 6,000-satellite constellation seen as China's answer to Starlink.

items.headline: CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury dies at 72
items.detail: Sitaram Yechury, General Secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) since 2015, died in New Delhi at the age of 72. He was the party's fifth General Secretary and a former Rajya Sabha MP from West Bengal.

items.headline: Polaris Dawn performs first private spacewalk
items.detail: The Polaris Dawn mission, commanded by billionaire Jared Isaacman, carried out the first commercial spacewalk on September 12, 2024. The Dragon spacecraft reached an apogee of about 1,400 km, the farthest humans have travelled since Apollo 17.

items.headline: Second successful test of VLSRSAM
items.detail: DRDO and the Indian Navy conducted the second consecutive flight test of the Vertical Launch Short Range Surface-to-Air Missile off the Odisha coast. The missile weighs about 170 kg and flies at Mach 4.5.

items.headline: Tarang Shakti-24: IAF's first multinational air exercise
items.detail: Phase II of Exercise Tarang Shakti-24, the Indian Air Force's first multinational air exercise, concluded at Jodhpur on September 14, 2024. It ran from August 29, 2024.

items.headline: World Ozone Day marks 30th observance
items.detail: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer was observed on September 16, 2024, with the theme 'Montreal Protocol: Advancing Climate Actions'.

items.headline: Navy clears Rs 2,500 crore plan for unmanned underwater vessels
items.detail: The Defence Ministry cleared the Indian Navy's Rs 2,500 crore plan to procure Extra-Large Unmanned Underwater Vessels (XLUUVs) weighing over 100 tonnes.

items.headline: NaBFID notified as a Public Financial Institution
items.detail: The Corporate Affairs Ministry notified the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) as a Public Financial Institution under the Companies Act, 2013, after consulting the RBI.

items.headline: Standard operating papers released for White Revolution 2.0
items.detail: Union Cooperation Minister Amit Shah released SOPs for 'White Revolution 2.0' in New Delhi under the theme 'Sahkar-se-Samriddhi' to strengthen the dairy sector through cooperatives.

items.headline: 6th Quad Leaders' Summit held in Wilmington
items.detail: The sixth Quad Leaders' Summit was hosted by US President Joe Biden at Wilmington, Delaware on September 21, 2024, with PM Modi, Anthony Albanese and Fumio Kishida attending. The Quad Cancer Moonshot, aimed at fighting cervical cancer, was launched.

items.headline: India win both titles at 45th Chess Olympiad
items.detail: India won gold in both the Open and Women's sections of the 45th Chess Olympiad held in Budapest, Hungary from September 10-22, 2024, becoming the third nation after the Soviet Union and China to win both titles at one Olympiad. The Open team scored a record 21/22 match points.
examFacts: India won Open and Women's gold

items.headline: Atishi sworn in as Delhi's Chief Minister
items.detail: AAP leader Atishi took oath as the 8th Chief Minister of Delhi on September 23, 2024, succeeding Arvind Kejriwal. She is Delhi's third woman Chief Minister.

items.headline: Anura Kumara Dissanayake wins Sri Lanka presidency
items.detail: Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the JVP-led alliance was sworn in as the 9th Executive President of Sri Lanka on September 23, 2024, winning about 42.31% of votes.

items.headline: Air Marshal Amar Preet Singh to be IAF Chief
items.detail: Air Marshal Amar Preet Singh was appointed the next Chief of the Air Staff, taking charge on September 30, 2024, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Vivek Ram Chaudhari.
examFacts: Next IAF Chief: Air Marshal Amar Preet Singh

quiz.q: How many medals did India win at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, its best-ever tally?
quiz.solution: India won 29 medals (7 gold, 9 silver, 13 bronze) and finished 18th.

quiz.q: At the 45th Chess Olympiad in Budapest, India won gold in:
quiz.solution: India became the third nation after the USSR and China to win both titles at one Olympiad.

quiz.q: Sitaram Yechury, who passed away in September 2024, was General Secretary of:
quiz.solution: He led the CPI(M) as its fifth General Secretary from 2015 to 2024.

quiz.q: Atishi became the Chief Minister of Delhi in September 2024. Which woman CM of Delhi was she?
quiz.solution: She is Delhi's third woman CM, after Sushma Swaraj and Sheila Dikshit.

quiz.q: The 6th Quad Leaders' Summit in September 2024 was hosted at:
quiz.solution: US President Joe Biden hosted the summit at Wilmington, Delaware on September 21, 2024.

quiz.q: Which mission carried out the world's first commercial (private) spacewalk in September 2024?
quiz.solution: Polaris Dawn, commanded by Jared Isaacman, performed the spacewalk; the craft reached about 1,400 km.

quiz.q: What is the strike range of the Agni-4 ballistic missile test-fired in September 2024?
quiz.solution: The nuclear-capable Agni-4 has a range of about 4,000 km and was tested from Chandipur.

quiz.q: Anura Kumara Dissanayake was elected the 9th Executive President of:
quiz.solution: He won about 42.31% of votes and was sworn in on September 23, 2024.

quiz.q: Who won the men's singles title at the US Open 2024?
quiz.solution: Jannik Sinner beat Taylor Fritz; Aryna Sabalenka won the women's title.

quiz.q: Odisha's CM-KISAN scheme, launched in September 2024, replaced which scheme?
quiz.solution: CM-KISAN replaced KALIA and gives small farmers Rs 4,000 a year.

items.headline: Four thematic hubs announced for National Quantum Mission
items.detail: Four thematic hubs with 14 technical groups and 152 researchers from 43 institutions were announced under the National Quantum Mission. The indigenous multimodal LLM 'Bharat Gen' was also launched.

items.headline: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission completes three years
items.detail: The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, launched on September 27, 2021, completed three years, with over 67 crore ABHA IDs created and 42 crore health records linked.

items.headline: World Bank approves Rs 15,000 crore for Amaravati
items.detail: The World Bank approved a Rs 15,000 crore loan, alongside ADB support, for building Amaravati, the capital city of Andhra Pradesh, part of a total Rs 49,000 crore project.

items.headline: 'eShram One Stop Solution' launched
items.detail: Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched the 'eShram One Stop Solution' portal, integrating services like ONORC, MGNREGA and PM-SYM for over 30 crore registered unorganised workers.

items.headline: Classical language status for five languages
items.detail: The Union Cabinet approved classical language status for Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali, taking the number of classical languages in India to eleven.
examFacts: New classical languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali

items.headline: DRDO flight-tests VSHORADS missiles at Pokhran
items.detail: DRDO conducted three successful flight tests of the fourth-generation VSHORADS, a very short-range air defence missile, at the Pokhran field firing ranges in Rajasthan, with a strike range of up to 6 km.

items.headline: MACE Observatory inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh
items.detail: The Major Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) Observatory, Asia's largest and the world's highest Cherenkov telescope, was inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh at about 4,300 m altitude. It was built by BARC with ECIL.
examFacts: Asia's largest, world's highest Cherenkov telescope

items.headline: World Space Week 2024 observed
items.detail: World Space Week was observed from October 4-10, 2024 with the theme 'Space and Climatic Change'.

items.headline: Nobel Prizes 2024 announced
items.detail: The 2024 Nobel Prizes were announced in October 2024. Physics went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for work on machine learning with artificial neural networks; Chemistry to David Baker, Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein design and prediction; Medicine to Victor Ambros and Gary Ruvkun for microRNA; Literature to Han Kang of South Korea; Peace to Japan's Nihon Hidankyo for a world free of nuclear weapons; and Economics to Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson and James Robinson for studies of institutions and prosperity.

items.headline: INS Nirdeshak delivered to Indian Navy
items.detail: Garden Reach Shipbuilders delivered INS Nirdeshak, the second of four Survey Vessel Large ships, to the Indian Navy on October 8, 2024. The 110 m ship has over 80% indigenous content.

items.headline: Partha Pratim Sengupta to lead Bandhan Bank
items.detail: The RBI approved Partha Pratim Sengupta, former MD & CEO of Indian Overseas Bank, as MD & CEO of Bandhan Bank for three years.
examFacts: Bandhan Bank MD & CEO: Partha Pratim Sengupta

items.headline: Ratan Tata passes away at 86
items.detail: Ratan Tata, Chairman Emeritus of the Tata Group, died in Mumbai on October 9, 2024 at the age of 86. He led Tata Sons from 1991 to 2012 and received the Padma Vibhushan in 2008. He was given a state funeral with military honours on October 10.

items.headline: ISSF World Cup Final held in New Delhi
items.detail: The ISSF World Cup Final 2024 was held from October 13-18 at the Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range, New Delhi. China topped the medals; India finished with four medals, including silver for Sonam Maskar in the women's 10m air rifle.

items.headline: NASA launches Europa Clipper to Jupiter's moon
items.detail: NASA launched the Europa Clipper mission on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center on October 14, 2024, its first mission dedicated to studying an ocean world beyond Earth, Jupiter's moon Europa.

items.headline: e-Migrate V2.0 portal and app launched
items.detail: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya launched the e-Migrate V2.0 portal and app for overseas Indian workers, with a 24/7 multilingual helpline and DigiLocker integration.

items.headline: India extends first rupee-denominated Line of Credit
items.detail: India extended a Rs 487.60 crore rupee-denominated Line of Credit to Mauritius for a water pipeline replacement project, its first fully rupee-based LoC under the IDEAS scheme.

items.headline: India sixth in global 6G patents
items.detail: As per MaxVal data, India ranked sixth in the world in 6G patents with 188 filings. China led with 6,001, followed by the USA, South Korea, Japan and the EU.

items.headline: India hosts first ITU Telecom Standardization Assembly
items.detail: PM Modi inaugurated the ITU World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (WTSA) 2024 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, held from October 15-24, 2024. It was the first WTSA in India and the Asia-Pacific region.

items.headline: Paramesh Sivamani becomes Coast Guard chief
items.detail: Paramesh Sivamani took over as the 26th Director General of the Indian Coast Guard on October 16, 2024.

items.headline: ISRO chief Somanath wins IAF World Space Award
items.detail: ISRO Chairman S. Somanath received the International Astronautical Federation's World Space Award at the 75th International Astronautical Congress held in Milan, Italy from October 14-18, 2024.

items.headline: New Zealand win first Women's T20 World Cup
items.detail: New Zealand beat South Africa by 32 runs in the final in Dubai on October 20, 2024 to win their first ICC Women's T20 World Cup. Amelia Kerr was Player of the Tournament and top wicket-taker with 15 wickets.
examFacts: Player of the Tournament: Amelia Kerr

items.headline: Prabowo Subianto sworn in as Indonesia's President
items.detail: Prabowo Subianto was sworn in as the 8th President of Indonesia on October 20, 2024, succeeding Joko Widodo, with Gibran Rakabuming Raka as Vice President.

items.headline: World Osteoporosis Day 2024 observed
items.detail: World Osteoporosis Day was observed on October 20, 2024 with the theme 'Say no to fragile bones'.

items.headline: General Luong Cuong elected Vietnam's President
items.detail: General Luong Cuong was elected the 14th President of Vietnam on October 21, 2024, succeeding To Lam.

quiz.q: Which organisation won the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize?
quiz.solution: Japan's Nihon Hidankyo won for its work towards a world free of nuclear weapons.

quiz.q: Which five languages received classical language status from the Cabinet in October 2024?
quiz.solution: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali were added, taking India's classical languages to 11.

quiz.q: Ratan Tata, who passed away in October 2024, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in which year?
quiz.solution: He received the Padma Vibhushan in 2008 (Padma Bhushan in 2000) and led Tata Sons from 1991 to 2012.

quiz.q: Which team won its first ICC Women's T20 World Cup title in October 2024?
quiz.solution: New Zealand beat South Africa by 32 runs in the Dubai final; Amelia Kerr was Player of the Tournament.

quiz.q: The MACE Observatory, the world's highest Cherenkov telescope, was inaugurated at:
quiz.solution: MACE was inaugurated at Hanle, Ladakh, at about 4,300 m altitude.

quiz.q: NASA's Europa Clipper, launched in October 2024, will study which Jupiter moon?
quiz.solution: Europa Clipper is NASA's first mission dedicated to studying an ocean world beyond Earth: Jupiter's moon Europa.

quiz.q: Prabowo Subianto was sworn in as President of which country in October 2024?
quiz.solution: He became Indonesia's 8th President, succeeding Joko Widodo.

quiz.q: India hosted the ITU World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (WTSA) for the first time in:
quiz.solution: WTSA 2024 was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi from October 15-24, 2024.

quiz.q: India's rank in global 6G patents, as per MaxVal data released in October 2024, was:
quiz.solution: India stood 6th with 188 patents; China topped with 6,001.

quiz.q: India extended its first-ever rupee-denominated Line of Credit to which country?
quiz.solution: A Rs 487.60 crore LoC went to Mauritius for a water pipeline project under the IDEAS scheme.

items.headline: JMM-led alliance wins Jharkhand assembly election
items.detail: The JMM-led alliance won a majority in the Jharkhand assembly elections held from November 13-20, 2024.

items.headline: Rani Rampal retires; jersey No. 28 retired
items.detail: Former India women's hockey captain Rani Rampal announced her retirement. She scored 205 goals in 254 matches, and Hockey India retired her No. 28 jersey.

items.headline: MUDRA loan limit doubled to Rs 20 lakh with 'Tarun Plus'
items.detail: A new 'Tarun Plus' category was introduced under the PM Mudra Yojana, allowing loans up to Rs 20 lakh for borrowers who had successfully repaid earlier Tarun loans.

items.headline: Operational guidelines released for Namo Drone Didi
items.detail: The agriculture ministry released guidelines for Namo Drone Didi, a Rs 1,261 crore scheme to provide drones to 14,500 women self-help groups for agricultural services.

items.headline: Kartarpur Corridor agreement extended till 2029
items.detail: India and Pakistan agreed to renew the Kartarpur Corridor agreement for five years till 2029. The corridor links Dera Baba Nanak in Punjab to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan.
examFacts: Links Dera Baba Nanak to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib

items.headline: Armenia joins International Solar Alliance
items.detail: Armenia became the 104th full member of the International Solar Alliance, effective November 15, 2024. The ISA is headquartered in Gurugram.

items.headline: Inter-State Council reconstituted
items.detail: The government reconstituted the Inter-State Council with PM Narendra Modi as chairman, state chief ministers and nine Union ministers as members.

items.headline: Solar-hydrogen microgrid inaugurated at Chushul, Ladakh
items.detail: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh virtually inaugurated an NTPC-made solar-hydrogen microgrid for the Indian Army at Chushul, Ladakh. It gives 200 kW round-the-clock power and works at minus 30 degrees C and 4,400 m altitude.

items.headline: Arvindar Singh Sahney appointed IOCL Chairman
items.detail: Arvindar Singh Sahney was appointed Chairman of Indian Oil Corporation Limited for a five-year term, succeeding Satish Kumar Vaduguri.

items.headline: Tayyab Ikram elected FIH President till 2032
items.detail: Mohammad Tayyab Ikram was elected the 13th President of the International Hockey Federation (FIH) at the 49th FIH Statutory Congress in Muscat, Oman, with a term till 2032.

items.headline: PRL discovers Saturn-sized exoplanet TOI-6651b
items.detail: Scientists at the Physical Research Laboratory discovered TOI-6651b, a Saturn-sized exoplanet about five times the size and 60 times heavier than Earth, using the PARAS-2 spectrograph. It was PRL's fourth exoplanet discovery.

items.headline: Elon Musk tops Fortune list of powerful business people
items.detail: Elon Musk topped Fortune's first '100 Most Powerful People in Business' list, with Jensen Huang second and Satya Nadella third. Mukesh Ambani was 12th, the only Indian on the list.

items.headline: India in top 10 for patents, trademarks and designs
items.detail: The World Intellectual Property Indicators 2024 report placed India among the top 10 countries in patents, trademarks and industrial designs.
examFacts: India: top 10 in patents, trademarks, designs

items.headline: 9th India-Indonesia exercise Garud Shakti held in Jakarta
items.detail: The 9th edition of the India-Indonesia joint special forces exercise Garud Shakti was held at Cijantung, Jakarta from November 1-12, 2024.

items.headline: 15th India-US exercise Vajra Prahar held in USA
items.detail: The 15th India-US joint special forces exercise Vajra Prahar was held at the Orchard Combat Training Centre, Idaho, USA from November 2-22, 2024, with 45 personnel from each side.

items.headline: New Zealand inflict first home Test series defeat on India
items.detail: India lost a home Test series to New Zealand in November 2024, its first home Test series defeat, with the final match ending on November 3.
examFacts: India's first home Test series defeat

items.headline: Verstappen wins Brazilian GP from 17th on grid
items.detail: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, Sao Paulo after starting 17th, his eighth win of the 2024 season.

items.headline: Donald Trump wins US presidential election
items.detail: Donald Trump was elected the 47th President of the United States in the November 5, 2024 election, becoming the first president to win non-consecutive terms since Grover Cleveland in 1892. JD Vance became Vice President.

items.headline: National Legal Services Day observed
items.detail: The 30th National Legal Services Day was observed on November 9, 2024, marking the launch of legal services under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.

items.headline: Justice Sanjiv Khanna sworn in as 51st CJI
items.detail: Justice Sanjiv Khanna was sworn in as the 51st Chief Justice of India on November 11, 2024, succeeding Justice D.Y. Chandrachud. He served until May 13, 2025.

items.headline: COP29 climate summit ends with new finance goal
items.detail: The UN climate conference COP29 was held in Baku, Azerbaijan from November 11-22, 2024. The 'Baku Finance Goal' was set to raise at least USD 1.3 trillion a year for developing nations, and carbon market rules under Article 6 were agreed.
examFacts: Finance goal: USD 1.3 trillion a year

items.headline: Vistara merges into Air India; airline ceases operations
items.detail: Vistara flew its last flight on November 11, 2024, ending operations after about nine years as it merged into Air India following the Tata group's merger plan.

items.headline: Supreme Court bans 'bulldozer' demolitions
items.detail: The Supreme Court ruled against the practice of demolishing homes of people accused of crimes, laying down pan-India guidelines for demolition by authorities.

items.headline: India successfully tests first hypersonic missile
items.detail: India test-fired its first hypersonic missile from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast on November 16, 2024, joining a small group of countries with this capability.
examFacts: Launch site: Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha

items.headline: National Press Day 2024 observed
items.detail: National Press Day was observed on November 16, 2024 with the theme 'Changing Nature of the Press', marking the Press Council of India starting work on November 16, 1966. India was ranked 159th of 180 countries in the RSF World Press Freedom Index 2024.

items.headline: Mahayuti wins landslide in Maharashtra assembly election
items.detail: The BJP-led Mahayuti alliance won a landslide victory in the Maharashtra assembly elections held in November 2024.

items.headline: ISRO, Australian space agency sign Gaganyaan agreement
items.detail: ISRO signed an Implementation Agreement with the Australian Space Agency on November 20, 2024 for cooperation in recovering Gaganyaan crew modules after landing.

items.headline: World Fisheries Day 2024 observed
items.detail: World Fisheries Day was observed on November 21, 2024. The Indian theme was 'India's Blue Transformation: Strengthening Small-scale and Sustainable Fisheries', and Kerala won the Best Marine State award.

items.headline: 4th edition of coastal defence exercise Sea Vigil
items.detail: The Indian Navy conducted the fourth edition of the biennial coastal defence exercise Sea Vigil-24 on November 20-21, 2024, covering India's 11,098 km coastline.

items.headline: 13-year-old becomes youngest IPL contract signee
items.detail: Thirteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest player to sign an IPL contract, joining Rajasthan Royals for Rs 1.1 crore at the mega auction.

quiz.q: Who was sworn in as the 51st Chief Justice of India in November 2024?
quiz.solution: Justice Sanjiv Khanna took oath on November 11, 2024, succeeding Justice D.Y. Chandrachud.

quiz.q: Donald Trump was elected as the ___ President of the United States in November 2024.
quiz.solution: Trump won the November 5, 2024 election to become the 47th US President; JD Vance became Vice President.

quiz.q: From where was India's first hypersonic missile test-fired in November 2024?
quiz.solution: The test was conducted from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast on November 16, 2024.

quiz.q: Vistara, which ceased operations in November 2024, merged with which airline?
quiz.solution: Vistara merged into Air India after about nine years of operations.

quiz.q: The COP29 UN climate conference in November 2024 was held in:
quiz.solution: COP29 was held in Baku; the Baku Finance Goal targets USD 1.3 trillion a year for developing nations.

quiz.q: Under the 'Tarun Plus' category announced in November 2024, the MUDRA loan limit was raised to:
quiz.solution: Tarun Plus allows loans up to Rs 20 lakh for successful past Tarun borrowers.

quiz.q: The Kartarpur Corridor agreement between India and Pakistan was extended till which year?
quiz.solution: The 2019 agreement was renewed for five years till 2029.
